$comment: THE FORTY PROOF CASES — eight towers x five crowd shapes, fixed forever.
docs/design/design_handoff_casual_mode/ENGINE_CONTRACT.md section 12.3 is the contract: one
list, three readers (the gauntlet, the ladder's 'What are the forty?' panel, and the bench's
suite). A rating is the mean of all forty, and the cases never move, so two ratings a month
apart stay comparable. That last clause is the whole reason this file exists in data/ rather
than as a constant: CLAUDE.md invariant 7 puts anything tunable in data, and a fixture list a
public rating is computed over is the strongest case of it. A second copy of these names
anywhere in packages/ is a defect, and gauntlet/proofCases.test.ts fails on one.
WHAT IS AUTHORED HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. Ids, rates, horizons and demand blocks are authored.
Building NAMES and specs are not: they are resolved from data/buildings/ at load, on
data/reference-runs.json's own ground -- a name authored beside an id is a second source of
truth that goes stale the day the building is edited. The 'why' line is authored, because it
is an argument about the set rather than a fact about the building.
THE EIGHT ARE NOT THE CONTRACT'S EIGHT, AND THE DEPARTURE IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.
Section 12.3 names Harbour Point (16 fl, 6 lifts) and Ashgate Mixed-Use (22 fl, 5 lifts).
Neither is in data/buildings/, and a case naming a building this build does not ship cannot
run -- a rating over 30 of 40 is not the rating section 12.3 defines, and substituting one
shipped building silently for another is the false-statement-about-the-thing-asked-after that
dev/main.ts#dispatcherNameOf refuses by name. So the two shipped buildings the contract does
not name -- mixed-use-high-rise and secure-tower -- take those two places, and this paragraph
is the record. The day either building is authored, it takes its place back and every rating
measured before that day stops being comparable with every rating measured after: that is what
'the cases never move' costs, and it is the reason moving one is a decision rather than an edit.
THE SPECS IN SECTION 12.3'S TABLE ARE THE PROTOTYPE'S AND ARE NOT REPRODUCED. It says Chancery
House is 14 floors and 3 lifts; data/buildings/chancery-house.json is 19 floors and 6 cars.
CLAUDE.md: the handoff wins every disagreement about what the screen looks like, and the
simulator wins every disagreement about what a number means. A floor count is a number.
THE RATES ARE PER TOWER AND THE SHAPES ARE PER CROWD, which is the one structural decision in
this file. A crowd shape is a directional split and a group shape -- properties of the people.
A level that fills a 101-floor tower empties a six-floor one, so the level belongs to the
building. Where a rate below is also a matrix cell's rate, benchmark/matrixCells.ts' rationale
for it is the reason and is cited; the rest are authored by analogy and say so.
WINDOWS ARE FULL-RUN ON ALL FORTY. The peak-5min window is empty often enough on the sparse
towers to invalidate the case (matrixCells.ts, garden-residential's rationale), and forty cases
reported over two different windows would be forty numbers under one label.
THE SEED RULES ARE NOT IN THIS FILE, AND THERE ARE TWO OF THEM. Section 1's table carries one
per reader over this one list: hash(towerId, crowdIndex) for the GAUNTLET, fixed forever, and
hash(testId, repIndex) for the BENCH, 'the same for every entrant -- that is what matched
crowds means'. They are computed in gauntlet/proofCases.ts#proofSeedOf and #benchSeedOf so that
a seed cannot be edited into incomparability by a hand that meant to change a rate. So 'one
list, three readers' is a claim about FIXTURES and never about traces -- and that is also
CLAUDE.md's hold-out discipline, since a bench sharing the gauntlet's seeds would let a player
tune a dispatcher against the exact forty runs it is about to be rated on. proofCases.test.ts
asserts the two seed SETS are disjoint over the shipped forty rather than trusting that two
hashes of different strings differ. Invariant 5 still holds -- every case carries the seed it
ran under, into the rating record. See DECISIONS.md sections D445 and D446.

towers.why: a short building where one lift out changes everything
sparse traffic, and idle cars in the wrong place
a credential on every call, so authorisation and dispatch meet on every decision
offices over homes on one stack, shuttles above locals, and no single crowd shape that suits both
zoning, and a genuine evening exodus
priority traffic that must survive ordinary traffic
a sky lobby, where parking is the whole game
